{"world_model":"W6 after E062. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost has a pixel-proportional compute part and a bandwidth/elementwise part (BN/GELU, ~27% of a 32 px step). The tip is E061: 5.0235 s, 0.7534 on seeds 0–2 (225 steps).

My E062 miss: Muon→SGD lost 2.9 pp, not 0.2–0.5. I had guessed that PR #3 (SGD beating Muon) and the E006 confound made Muon roughly neutral. Instead Muon is load-bearing in this short, 225-step, momentum-0.6, batch-2000 regime. The saving was 0.28 s, more than the 0.8 ms per step I expected. So H1.2 is supported here. Lesson: optimizer-axis swaps are far from neutral. Don't extrapolate from the airbench SGD recipe.

Mechanisms and supporting experiments:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 0.8–2.5 s/pp. Step, epoch and sample cuts trade near that dial (E020, E031, E040, E041, E045, E048, E061). Early 20 px steps look cheap on unselected seeds (E061).
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail carries accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share, because it also skips BN/GELU backward and optimizer traffic (E028, E036, E046, E049). It is free only after the block has finished learning (E037, E054, E055).
4. Activation cost is partly compute-bound. ReLU saved 0.25 s but lost 0.54 pp (E056). Smoothness matters. A tanh-GELU or SiLU swap likely saves less than 1.5%.
5. Averaging variants, LS late, warm-up, Lookahead interval and BN recalibration are null or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044). wd ×0.5 gave about +0.2 pp. The recipe is near a local optimum.
6. Architecture surgery on high-resolution work loses more than it saves (E051). Width and conv removal trade at roughly the dial's rate or worse.
7. Noise: the 3-seed mean moves ±0.2 pp across rebuilds, and time moves ±0.03–0.1 s. Seed-set winner's curse is 0.1–0.2 pp. The unselected population mean is about 0.752–0.754, so the margin over 0.75 is thin.

Unsure: the true rebuild SD, whether coarse labels are usable (likely not), PCIe transfer, and how far the early-trim dose stays free.

My E062 miss: Muon→SGD lost 2.9 pp, not 0.2–0.5. I had guessed that PR #3 (SGD beating Muon) and the E006 confound made Muon roughly neutral. Instead Muon is load-bearing in this short, 225-step, momentum-0.6, batch-2000 regime. The saving was 0.28 s, more than the 0.8 ms per step I expected. So H1.2 is supported here. Lesson: optimizer-axis swaps are far from neutral. Don't extrapolate from the airbench SGD recipe.

Mechanisms and supporting experiments:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 0.8–2.5 s/pp. Step, epoch and sample cuts trade near that dial (E020, E031, E040, E041, E045, E048, E061). Early 20 px steps look cheap on unselected seeds (E061).
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail carries accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share, because it also skips BN/GELU backward and optimizer traffic (E028, E036, E046, E049). It is free only after the block has finished learning (E037, E054, E055).
4. Activation cost is partly compute-bound. ReLU saved 0.25 s but lost 0.54 pp (E056). Smoothness matters. A tanh-GELU or SiLU swap likely saves less than 1.5%.
5. Averaging variants, LS late, warm-up, Lookahead interval and BN recalibration are null or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044). wd ×0.5 gave about +0.2 pp. The recipe is near a local optimum.
6. Architecture surgery on high-resolution work loses more than it saves (E051). Width and conv removal trade at roughly the dial's rate or worse.
7. Noise: the 3-seed mean moves ±0.2 pp across rebuilds, and time moves ±0.03–0.1 s. Seed-set winner's curse is 0.1–0.2 pp. The unselected population mean is about 0.752–0.754, so the margin over 0.75 is thin.

Unsure: the true rebuild SD, whether coarse labels are usable (likely not), PCIe transfer, and how far the early-trim dose stays free.

Expectations: I099 saves about 0.12 s for −0.1 pp, so it is marginal. I100, I101 and I102 sit near the dial. I103 is neutral to slightly positive.

forecasts.reason: Offline step likely shows tanh-GELU/SiLU savings under 1.5%, so the activation branch closes; if run, it is near neutral.
Saves about 0.12 s, costs about 0.1 pp; the gate is thin and the result is noise-limited.
Group-3 width cut loses about 0.3 pp for a ~0.14 s saving, about the dial's rate or worse, and fails the gate.
Removing a conv in the stem group costs capacity and saves modestly; E051-style stem surgery lost.
Early-phase res change is cheap, saving about 0.05 s for about −0.1 pp; within noise.
LS 0.2 vs 0.3 was flat at E013; 0.15 is likely within ±0.1 pp.

cruxes: Do the early 20 px steps stay nearly free below 225 steps (I099), or does E061's −0.02 pp reflect noise?
Does the accuracy gate (μ̂ − 1.64σ ≥ 0.75) pass on the PCIe judge given rebuild SD, which sets how much margin can be spent on cuts?
Do tanh-GELU or SiLU keep GELU's accuracy while recovering a meaningful part of ReLU's 0.25 s saving?
